Subject: Redwood Private / VPC — follow-up & next tests

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

- What we heard: Acme Health needs a private inference option for PHI workloads with strict network isolation, company-controlled KMS, and the ability to operate in an air-gapped / on-prem configuration for selected sites. Primary success metrics are: sub-100ms tail latency for 2k token contexts for critical routes, predictable throughput for batch scoring (100 req/s), and clear auditability (audit logs + retention policy).

- How Redwood maps to that: Redwood Private supports a VPC-deployed control plane (customer VPC peering / PrivateLink options) and an on-prem / air-gapped package where the control plane can be run in a private network. We also support external KMS/HSM integrations and audit log forwarding.

- Immediate asks / next tests we proposed on the call:
  1) Provide your network inventory and outbound egress constraints so our infra team can validate connectivity; attached: networking_requirements_v1.pdf and a short architecture diagram (redwood-private-architecture.png).
  2) Run a short baseline latency test against a small model (BLOOM-350M equivalent) from a representative Acme environment — we can provide a test harness and container.
  3) Validate KMS integration requirements (key wrapping, rotation windows, HSM endpoints).
  4) Confirm whether complete air-gap (no external internet after provisioning) is required or if a staged provisioning flow (provision then disconnect) is acceptable.

Proposed immediate next step: 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra/security and our solutions + SE team to nail the network/PKI details. I’m available next Wed/Thu afternoon (PST) — please propose a slot.

Attaching: redwood-private-architecture.png, networking_requirements_v1.pdf (stubs).

Thanks — vanessa

- Competitor concerns: our infra folks want a short note on how Redwood Private differs from deploying a model on a hyperscaler endpoint (e.g., SageMaker / Azure ML) and from vendor-hosted inference APIs (latency, control plane exposure, pricing predictability). Any collateral is helpful.

Jordan — looping in some technical details to address the infra/security asks. High level differences vs hyperscalers and hosted inference APIs:

- Control plane & network exposure: Hyperscaler-managed endpoints typically expose a control plane that lives on the cloud provider network; even with VPC endpoints there's still a managed control plane surface. Redwood Private supports two patterns: (1) Customer VPC + private control plane (control plane endpoints accessible only via your VPC / PrivateLink), and (2) Fully private on-prem bundle where the control plane is deployed inside your network and does not call out externally after provisioning. For the fully air-gapped option we ship the runtime, management tools, and signed upgrade artifacts; update cadence is agreed in the SOW.

- KMS/HSM integration: We support tenant-managed keys via KMIP or external cloud KMS (customer-provided). For HSMs we integrate via PKCS#11 or KMIP depending on vendor — our SEs have run integrations with Thales/HSM appliances and cloud HSMs. We can run a short key exchange test during the POC.

- Latency & cost predictability: Because the runtime is colocated in your VPC or on-prem, token-level latency is comparable to local-hosted inference and we can tune kernel selection / quantization to meet latency SLOs. Compared to hyperscalers, our focus is on deterministic serving (continuous batching, KV caching) and cost levers that are visible to you (batch size, quantization profile, cache TTLs).

Suggested next technical tests for POC (order of execution):
  1) Network validation: our infra will validate egress/ingress rules with the attachments you provided.
  2) KMS handshake: smoke test with your HSM endpoint (PKCS#11) or KMIP.
  3) Baseline latency run: small model, then scaled to your target model; measure p50/p95/p99 for 512/2k token contexts.
  4) Throughput burst test: sustained 100 req/s with realistic prompt mix.
  5) Air-gap simulation: provision in a staging VPC, then cut external access and validate model serving and logs locally.

Attachments: airgap_playbook_v1.pdf (stub), SOC2_report_excerpt.pdf (excerpt for security review).

Happy to present a short one-pager to your security team that pulls these points together; Vanessa / Marissa — do you want me to draft that?

Thanks — Aditya
